claims.statement: TypeSpec is the core domain model for Java types, containing fields for kind (CLASS/INTERFACE/ENUM), name, annotations, modifiers, type variables, superclass and superinterfaces, enum constants, field specs, static/initializer blocks, method specs, nested type specs, originating reflection elements, and always-qualified names.

CodeWriter uses a two-pass import collection algorithm: the first pass collects all needed imports using a nullAppendable sentinel (a no-op output target), then the second pass writes code with resolved imports based on what was collected.
The format string engine uses $L for literals (no escaping) and $S for quoted strings. The placeholder $T references types, which triggers automatic import emission.
JavaFile automatically creates the complete package directory hierarchy using Files.createDirectories() on each package component when writing to disk.
All file writes use UTF-8 charset by default; JavaFile.writeToPath() explicitly uses StandardCharsets.UTF_8 for encoding.
Nested types' simple names are collected into always-qualified name sets that prevent accidental shadowing when emitting code, especially important for nested types like java.util.Map.Entry.
JavaPoet validates argument types eagerly at builder construction time using checkArgument and checkState utilities, failing fast with descriptive errors before any code is generated.

The CodeWriter's NameAllocator resolves types by finding the shortest suffix that matches, considering local type names (for nested access like Map.Entry), imported types, and always-qualified exceptions to prevent collisions.
